title: Direct image commutes with base change along field extensions
statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of fields and $g:T\to S$ a
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated morphism of schemes over $K$; denote
$g_L:T_L\to S_L$ the base change to $\Spec(L)$. Let
$E\in\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ have cohomology sheaves whose stalks are
torsion of orders invertible in $K$, and let $E_L$ be the pullback
of $E$ to $(T_L)_{\Et}$. Then $Rg_{L,*}E_L$ is the pullback of
$Rg_*E$ to $S_L$.
(*Source:* Stacks Project,
[Tag `0F1C`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1C); the proof
below follows the reduction recorded there.)

proof.text: Write $a:S_L\to S$ and $b:T_L\to T$ for the projections. We prove that the canonical exchange $\beta_{L/K}(E):a^{-1}Rg_*E\to Rg_{L,*}b^{-1}E$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is invertible. First suppose $L/K$ is separable in the general field-extension sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], which allows transcendental extensions. By [lem-kun-separable-smooth-colimit], there is a nonempty small directed set of finitely generated smooth $K$-subalgebras $A_i\subset L$, with inclusions as transitions, such that $\operatorname{Spec}L=\varprojlim_i\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. The index is small because its objects are a subset of the set of subalgebras of the fixed field $L$. Nonemptiness and a common upper bound for any two indices are part of the filtered subalgebra presentation in that statement; inclusions make its index category a directed poset.

proof.text: Put $S_i=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. Each $S_i\to S$ is smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Each $\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is affine: the only opens of the field spectrum are the empty scheme and the whole target, whose preimages are affine. The transition maps $\operatorname{Spec}A_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ are affine by the inverse-limit clause of [lem-kun-separable-smooth-colimit] already invoked in Step 1; their targets need not be field spectra. Hence $S_i\to S$ and every transition $S_j\to S_i$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and $S_i\to S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The scheme $S_L$ is their inverse limit: for any test scheme $Z$, in a compatible family $Z\to S_i$, the composites to $S$ are all equal, since any two indices have a common upper bound. Hence such a family is precisely a single map $Z\to S$ and compatible maps $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, with equal composites to $\operatorname{Spec}K$. The latter maps are exactly a map $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ by Step 1, so the pair is exactly a map $Z\to S_L$. This establishes existence of the required limit directly; no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of the scheme $S$ itself is assumed.

proof.text: Fix any integer $q$, geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, and element $v\in\mathcal H^q(E)_{\bar t}$. Unpacking the stalkwise invertible-order clause of the current [def-kun-torsion-invertible], the hypothesis gives $n\in I_K=\{m\geq1:m\cdot1_K\ne0\}$ with $nv=0$; equivalently $n\cdot1_K$ is a unit in the field $K$. This is an elementwise condition: $n$ may depend on $q$, $\bar t$ and $v$. We use this clause directly and do not require one integer to kill a whole sheaf, a stalk, or all cohomology sheaves. The structure morphism $S\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ induces a unital ring map $K\to\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. The image of $(n\cdot1_K)^{-1}$ is a global inverse of $n\cdot1$, since a unital ring map preserves the equality $(n\cdot1_K)(n\cdot1_K)^{-1}=1$. This verifies exactly the elementwise global-unit condition in the current statement of [lem-kun-0f09], with no common annihilator required. Apply that node with base scheme $S$, direct-image morphism $f=g:T\to S$, and the nonempty small directed inverse system $(S_i\to S)$ of Steps 1 and 2. Its limit is $S'=S_L$ and the pulled-back source is $T\times_SS_L=T_L$. Every remaining hypothesis holds: $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by assumption, all stage maps are smooth and quasi-compact and quasi-separated, all transition maps are affine, and $E$ is bounded below. Its canonical exchange is exactly $\beta_{L/K}(E)$, so this proves the theorem for every separable $L/K$.

proof.text: For arbitrary $L/K$, use [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-purely-inseparable-overfield] for $K$ and $L$ to choose perfect purely inseparable overfields $K'/K$ and $L'/L$. They can be made compatible with the given embedding $K\hookrightarrow L$. In characteristic zero both overfields equal their base fields, and use the original embedding. In characteristic $p>0$, for $x\in K'$ choose $n$ with $x^{p^n}\in K$ and send $x$ to the unique $p^n$th root in $L'$ of the image of $x^{p^n}$. Such roots exist by perfectness of $L'$ and are unique because $u^{p^n}=v^{p^n}$ implies $(u-v)^{p^n}=0$ in a field. Increasing to a common exponent proves independence of $n$ and preservation of sums and products, using $(u+v)^{p^n}=u^{p^n}+v^{p^n}$ in characteristic $p$; the map preserves $1$, is therefore injective, and extends $K\hookrightarrow L$. We thus have a commuting diagram $K\to K'\to L'$ and $K\to L\to L'$.

proof.text: For every finitely generated intermediate field $K'\subset F\subset L'$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis]: $K'$ has characteristic zero or surjective Frobenius, and $F/K'$ is finitely generated as a field, so it has a finite transcendence basis over which it is separable algebraic. Consequently $L'/K'$ is separable by clause (2) of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. This uses general separability, not the assertion that $L'/K'$ is algebraic and not the definition of a separably closed field.

proof.text:
Let $q_T:T_{K'}\to T$, $q_S:S_{K'}\to S$, $v_T:T_{L'}\to T_L$ and $v_S:S_{L'}\to S_L$ be the projections. Each is a universal homeomorphism: by [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep] every test base change $Z\to T$, $S$, $T_L$ or $S_L$ is again the homeomorphism $Z_{K'}\to Z$ or $Z_{L'}\to Z$ for the same purely inseparable field extension, which is the definition [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], their inverse images are equivalences compatible with direct images, cohomology and composition. These identifications extend to bounded below derived categories: exact equivalences have exact inverses and preserve injectives, since $\operatorname{Hom}(-,FI)=\operatorname{Hom}(F^{-1}(-),I)$ is exact for injective $I$. Choose a bounded below injective representative $I$ of $E$ as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] makes every bounded below complex of injectives K-injective. The termwise complex $q_T^{-1}I$ is bounded below injective, so it is K-injective and can itself be the target resolution, with comparison map the identity. For an object $C$ of $\Dplus((T_L)_{\Et})$, choose a bounded below injective representative $J$; exactness and preservation of injectives by $v_T^{-1}$ make $v_T^{-1}J$ bounded below injective and hence K-injective by that clause, again with identity target-resolution comparison. For abelian sheaves $F$ on $T_{\Et}$ and $G$ on $(T_L)_{\Et}$, let $\gamma_K(F):q_S^{-1}g_*F\to g_{K',*}q_T^{-1}F$ and $\gamma_L(G):v_S^{-1}g_{L,*}G\to g_{L',*}v_T^{-1}G$ be the canonical maps of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], and write $\eta_u$ for the unit of $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$. Under the direct-image composition identifications obtained by associating the fibre products in the section formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the section formula in [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] gives
$$q_{S,*}(\gamma_K(F))\circ\eta_{q_S,g_*F}=g_*(\eta_{q_T,F}),\qquad v_{S,*}(\gamma_L(G))\circ\eta_{v_S,g_{L,*}G}=g_{L,*}(\eta_{v_T,G}).$$
Indeed, for an etale $W\to S$ both sides of the first equation send $s\in F(W\times_ST)$ to its inverse-image section on $(W\times_ST)\times_TT_{K'}$; the representative in the exchange formula is $W$ with the identity map $W\times_SS_{K'}\to W\times_SS_{K'}$. For an etale $V\to S_L$ both sides of the second equation send $t\in G(V\times_{S_L}T_L)$ to its inverse-image section on $(V\times_{S_L}T_L)\times_{T_L}T_{L'}$; here the representative is $V$ with the identity map $V\times_{S_L}S_{L'}\to V\times_{S_L}S_{L'}$. All four units are invertible because these horizontal inverse/direct-image adjunctions are equivalences by topological invariance. The two displayed equations therefore make $q_{S,*}(\gamma_K(F))$ and $v_{S,*}(\gamma_L(G))$ invertible. Their direct-image functors are equivalences and reflect isomorphisms, so $\gamma_K(F)$ and $\gamma_L(G)$ are invertible. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise], the maps $\gamma_K(I^r)$ and $\gamma_L(J^r)$ applied termwise to the injective representatives, with $j=\mathrm{id}$, compute the derived canonical exchanges and make them invertible: $\delta_K:q_S^{-1}Rg_*\to Rg_{K',*}q_T^{-1}$ and $\delta_L:v_S^{-1}Rg_{L,*}\to Rg_{L',*}v_T^{-1}$; they are the exchanges of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], because the equivalences carry the adjunction units and counits in its mate formula to the corresponding units and counits. Put $E_{K'}=q_T^{-1}E$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] and [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], its cohomology is $q_T^{-1}\mathcal H^r(E)$ and it is bounded below. The stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies these stalks with stalks of $\mathcal H^r(E)$; for each element the annihilator $n\in I_K$ from [def-kun-torsion-invertible] still annihilates its identified stalk element, and the ring map $K\to K'$ sends the inverse of $n\cdot1_K$ to the inverse of $n\cdot1_{K'}$. Thus the same $n$ belongs to $I_{K'}$, verifying the required stalkwise invertible-order condition after pullback, again without a common annihilator. Finally $g_{K'}$ remains quasi-compact and quasi-separated by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

proof.text:
Write $a':S_{L'}\to S_{K'}$ and $b':T_{L'}\to T_{K'}$. Apply the separable case of Step 3 to $L'/K'$, $g_{K'}$ and $E_{K'}$, whose hypotheses were checked in Steps 5 and 6, obtaining an isomorphism $\beta':(a')^{-1}Rg_{K',*}E_{K'}\to Rg_{L',*}(b')^{-1}E_{K'}$. The two paths from $S_{L'}$ to $S$ agree: $a\circ v_S=q_S\circ a'$, and similarly $b\circ v_T=q_T\circ b'$. The horizontal pasting formula, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting], applied to these two factorizations gives, after the inverse-image composition identifications,
$$\delta_L(E_L)\circ v_S^{-1}\bigl(\beta_{L/K}(E)\bigr)=\beta'\circ(a')^{-1}\bigl(\delta_K(E)\bigr).$$
Here $E_L=b^{-1}E$, and the targets are identified using $v_T^{-1}E_L=(b')^{-1}E_{K'}$. The right side is invertible and $\delta_L(E_L)$ is invertible, so $v_S^{-1}(\beta_{L/K}(E))$ is invertible. The functor $v_S^{-1}$ is an equivalence by [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], hence reflects isomorphisms. Therefore $\beta_{L/K}(E)$ itself is invertible, as required.

tool_uses.why: Clause (2), stability of smoothness under arbitrary base change, is a generic scheme-morphism tool used to construct the smooth stages over S; no lemma in this unit supplies that permanence statement.
Purely inseparable scalar extension gives a homeomorphism for every test scheme, supplying the universal-homeomorphism hypothesis for the existing topological-invariance route.
Topological invariance is the generic etale-topos tool explicitly required by the blueprint perfect-closure reduction.
Exact inverse image supplies preservation of cohomology and of the bounded-below coefficient condition, independently of the geometric base-change theorem.
Its stalk isomorphism ensures that pulling the coefficient to K-prime preserves the given torsion orders; no stalk computation is being replaced by a definition.
The horizontal pasting identity compares the original canonical exchange with the perfect-closure exchange along the two equal composites; the unit has no such pasting identity.
